s14.instructions: Can `anchor.statement` be understood and applied by a reader who has only the statement, without outside context? Ordinary technical terms, commands, flags, paths, environment variables, file formats, streams, and concrete prohibitions or conditions need no outside context. Outside context is needed when a decisive term is a subjective quality (such as robust), a private label or code with no definition (such as R7), or a person's approval with no identified record. Who is told to act (a named component, 'you', or nobody) and how the sentence is phrased never create an outside-context dependency. Ignore grammar, bundling, fidelity, and scope.

criteria.yes: Every decisive term is ordinary technical language or concrete content, so the statement applies without outside context.
criteria.no: A decisive term is a subjective quality, an undefined private label or code, or an approval with no identified record.
criteria.unclear: A term might depend on outside context, but it is not clear whether it is decisive.

s16.instructions: Can each decisive term in `anchor.statement` be understood from the statement itself or from common technical knowledge? Understood terms include commands, subcommands, flags, files, paths, values, environment variables, formats, streams, roles such as 'the caller', and terms the statement defines inline. How many concrete records the statement names (several paths, commit hashes, error or diagnostic codes, report ids) does not matter; each named record is understood on its own. Bundled duties, added details, sentence form, and who is told to act (a named component, 'you', or nobody) do not matter here. A term cannot be understood when it is a subjective quality (robust), a label or mode the statement never defines (R7, Mode K), an expected output or standard whose record the statement does not identify, or a person's approval with no identified record.

criteria.no: A decisive term is a subjective quality, an undefined label or mode, an unidentified expected output or standard, or an approval with no identified record.
criteria.unclear: A term may not be understood, but it cannot be told whether it is decisive.
criteria.yes: Every decisive term can be understood from the statement or common technical knowledge.

s17.instructions: Look at each term in `anchor.statement` that decides compliance, one at a time. A term is understood when it is a command, subcommand, flag, file or directory path, commit hash, error or diagnostic code, report or record id, value, environment variable, format, stream, a role such as 'the caller', or a term the statement defines inline; a statement may name many such records and still be fully understood. A term is not understood when it is a subjective quality (robust, clean), a label, tier, or mode the statement never defines (R7, Mode K), an expected output or standard whose record the statement does not identify, or a person's approval with no identified record. Sentence form, who is told to act, bundled duties, and details beyond the quote do not matter here.

criteria.yes: Every term that decides compliance is understood.
criteria.no: At least one term that decides compliance is a subjective quality, an undefined label, tier, or mode, an unidentified expected output or standard, or an approval with no identified record.
criteria.unclear: A term may not be understood, but it cannot be told whether it decides compliance.
